title: Discussion: Demystifying Agentic AI
html:
This discussion area is an additional means to interact with the weekly discussion and interactions. Please feel free to discuss our weekly topic live during the class session, via teams during the session, and/or here at any time during the week.

Additionally, groups can choose to present their weekly homework topics here if they choose to do so.

  1. Before the first meeting of the week:
    • Provide a substantive post reflecting on the reading materials and slide deck:
      1. One concept that was interesting to you and how you can apply it to your future career or life.
      2. One concept that was difficult to understand and what made it confusing.
      3. One external resource you found that helped you understand the concept better, along with an explanation of how it helped.
    • (Optional) Contribute to the group aspect of the weekly assignment.
  2. After the first meeting and before the second meeting of the week:
    • View and respond to the course recording.
    • Provide a written version of the in-class activities prior to the second meeting of the week AND
    • Respond to at least one peer to continue the conversation, clarify an idea, or share a relevant resource (you can respond to live session discussion points or online posts).
  3. Complete the weekly assignment.

Weekly Discussion Prompts: Demystifying Agentic AI

Use the prompts below to anchor your initial post, guide group collaboration, or prepare your responses:

Prompt 1: From Passive LLMs to Autonomous Agents

  • Context: Traditional LLMs operate on single-turn request-response cycles: they wait for human input, predict tokens, and stop. Agentic AI introduces autonomous perception-action loops, internal memory, and goal-directed behavior, allowing models to decompose high-level objectives and execute multi-step workflows without constant prompting.
  • Discussion Question: Identify a repetitive digital workflow in your current studies, job, or everyday life (e.g., scheduling, customer onboarding, research synthesis). How does an agentic loop handle edge cases and shifting conditions where traditional script automation fails?

Prompt 2: Tool Use and External API Grounding

  • Context: Foundation models are frozen in time and cannot interact with live environments on their own. By equipping agents with tools (REST APIs, code interpreters, vector databases, terminal commands), they can fetch real-time facts and make state changes in external systems.
  • Discussion Question: What is the biggest risk when giving an agent access to external write-tools (such as sending emails, executing shell commands, or writing to databases)? What architectural safeguards (e.g., human-in-the-loop gates, permission tiers) should an engineer implement?

Prompt 3: Reflex vs. Goal-Based and Utility-Based Architectures

  • Context: In classical AI, agents range from simple reflex agents (if-then rules) to model-based, goal-based, and utility-based systems. Modern agentic AI pairs these classical decision architectures with the contextual reasoning of LLMs.
  • Discussion Question: Select one real-world domain (such as autonomous robotics, automated financial trading, or healthcare triage). Would you deploy a goal-based agent or a utility-based agent, and how would it weigh competing trade-offs (e.g., speed vs. safety vs. cost)?

Prompt 4: Group Homework Topic Presentations (Optional)

  • If your group is choosing to present your weekly assignment findings here on the board, please share your slide link, code/workflow summary, and a brief overview of the problem you solved. Group members must reply within the thread to document individual contributions.
